description: Upload an audio track into a project from a public http(s) URL or a file attached in the chat, fetched server-side — the ONLY way to get an audio file's bytes into a project over MCP/HTTP (add_audio_overlay / update_audio_overlay only reference a file that is already uploaded). Pass `url` for a public http(s) link, or `file` for a file the person attached in the chat (a host that supports file inputs, such as ChatGPT, fills `file` with a temporary download link itself; do not ask the person for a URL to something they have attached). The target is the URL you pass and nothing else: Morpha's Worker fetches it with a plain HTTP GET, following redirects, and identifies itself as "Morpha/1.0 (+https://morphareels.ai; hello@morphareels.ai)". No third-party API is involved. The worker downloads the .mp3/.m4a/.wav/.ogg/.aac, stores it in the project's asset bucket under a new id, and returns { filename, name, sizeBytes, contentType }. Then pass the returned `filename` (the file's id, never shown to a person) to add_audio_overlay (add a second track) or update_audio_overlay { id, filename } (replace an existing track's file — find the id via describe_video's audio_overlays), with `name` as the track's name. A url must be a direct, publicly-fetchable http(s) link (not an auth-walled page). Buffered in Worker memory, so capped at 50 MB. A file on the person's own disk is uploaded in the editor. Reference: https://morphareels.ai/docs/tools#uploadaudiourl-file-name

file.description: A file the person attached in the chat (a host that supports file inputs, such as ChatGPT, fills this itself; do not type it). Pass either this or `url`.

download_url.description: Temporary URL the host serves the file at.

file_id.description: The host's id for the file.

file_name.description: The file's own name, when the host knows it.

mime_type.description: The file's media type, when the host knows it.

name.description: Optional display name, what people see (e.g. Theme.mp3). Defaults to the attached file's name or the URL's file name. It never decides where the file is stored.

projectId.description: Project to add the audio to.

url.description: Direct, publicly-fetchable http(s) URL of the audio file (.mp3/.m4a/.wav/.ogg/.aac). Pass either this or `file`.
